title: Trail Tool Fob (3 fold-out tools on one pin)
description: A swiss-knife style fob with three swing-out tools, no blades: a guy-line hook with cord-tie notches, a double hex wrench/pry bar (8 and 10 mm), and a 60 mm ruler arm. Two side plates, three arms and one pin.
use: Pocket tool for camping: tighten wing-nuts and bike/tent hardware, hook tent guy-lines, measure line and knot spacing.
material: PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 5 perimeters, 100% infill on arms (they are only 2.6 mm thick). The wrench is for light hand-tightening only.

problem_solved: Camp hardware (wing-nuts, tent line adjusters, cord) is usually handled with several loose bits; this folds guy-line hook, small wrench and ruler into one 70 x 26 x 14 mm fob with no blades.
mechanism: Three arms stacked on one 5 mm pin between two plates; arms swing outward away from the post side (0 to -180 deg). Friction between the 0.3 mm gapped layers holds them in place.
tolerances: Pin 2.5 mm radius: press (2.6 hole, +0.1) in plates, free (2.85, +0.35) in arms; 0.3 mm vertical gaps between layers; arms clear the posts by >= 2 mm; posts press 2.0 into 2.1 holes.
assembly: 1. Press the pin head-down through plate A, then slide the three arms over it (hook, wrench, ruler).
2. Fit plate B so the posts enter its holes (press fit), pushing the pin top through plate B.
3. A drop of glue on the pin top and post ends makes it permanent.
fit_notes: Small parts (pin, posts). Hex slots sized 8.2 / 10.2 mm across flats for easy fit.
